questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who __had look to__ rent an apartment in the city.
questions.solution:
The correct substitution is: **were looking to**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace "**had look to**" with "**were looking to**" to correct the sentence.
 
• "Were looking to" is the past continuous tense of the verb "to look." It is used to describe an ongoing action in the past. In this case, the action of looking for an apartment was ongoing in the past.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 
• "is looking to" - This option changes the verb tense from past to present. The sentence would read, "It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who are looking to rent an apartment in the city." **This option is not appropriate** because the sentence is describing an action that took place in the past, not the present.
 
• "No substitution required" - This option suggests that the original underlined segment is grammatically correct and does not require any changes. However, as mentioned earlier, "had look to" is not a correct phrase in English, so **this option is not appropriate.**
 
• "were looking for" - This option changes the verb "to rent" to "to look for." The sentence would read, "It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who were looking for an apartment in the city." This option changes the meaning of the sentence slightly. "Looking for" implies that they were searching for an apartment but hadn't yet found one, whereas "looking to rent" implies that they were actively seeking an apartment to rent.
 
• **"were looking to" - This option changes the verb tense to the past continuous, which is appropriate for describing an ongoing action in the past. The sentence would read, "It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who were looking to rent an apartment in the city." This option is the most appropriate because it corrects the grammatical error and accurately conveys the intended meaning.**

**Corrected sentence:*** It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who **were looking to__** rent an apartment in the city. *

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The girl ran into the house to get some ______ of bread, cold potatoes and other such morsels as were suitable for the fowls.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **crumbs**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The words given in options are called** collective nouns.**
 
• A collective noun is a noun that refers to some sort of group or collective—of people, animals, things, etc.
 
• Collective nouns are normally not treated as plural, even though they refer to a group of something.
 
• Let's look at the options given.
 
 
• **Heaps **mean an untidy pile of something. (वस्‍तुओं का अव्‍यवस्थित ढेर)
 
 
• **Example -** *Heaps of garbage*
 
 
 
• **Shells **mean a hard covering that protects eggs, nuts and some animals. (एक कठोर आवरण जो अंडे, नट और कुछ जानवरों की रक्षा करता है)
 
 
• **Example - ***A midden of shells*
 
 
 
• Crumbs mean a very small dry piece of bread, cake or biscuit. (ब्रेड, केक या बिस्किट का एक बहुत छोटा सूखा टुकड़ा)
 
 
• Example - *Crumbs of bread*
 
 
 
• **Bars **mean a straight piece of wood or metal that is longer than it is wide. (लकड़ी या धातु का एक सीधा टुकड़ा जो चौड़ा होने की तुलना में लंबा होता है) 
 
 
• **Example -** *Bars of gold.*
 
 
 
 

​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Complete sentence:** *The girl ran into the house to get some crumbs of bread__, cold potatoes, and other such morsels as were suitable for the fowls. *

Officials said thousands of office-goers were ________ the Metro, and the trains were running full during peak hours.

• **Running **means the action or sport of running. (दौड़ की क्रिया या खेल)

As per the meaning of the given words, "**taking**" is the most appropriate option to fill in.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Complete sentence:** *Officials said thousands of office-goers were taking __the Metro, and the trains were running full during peak hours. *

• In the present tense, we always use modal verbs with base verbs.
 
• So, when we use "**be**" with modal verbs like can, could, will, would, must, or should to name a few, we don’t have to change it.
